rationale: Open and execute a fifth, safety-shaped question on context validity: a configuration change whose log write fails is still installed in the leader's in-memory latest configuration, which then sizes quorums and elections. The harness fails exactly that write on a real two-voter cluster and records whether the node later commits a client command that the other voter never received.

investigations.question: When a leader's log write for a configuration change fails, is the new configuration still installed in memory, and can the node then elect itself and commit client entries with a quorum that the committed configuration does not recognise?
investigations.hypothesis: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry and then unconditionally calls setLatestConfiguration, commitment.setConfiguration and startStopReplication with the new configuration at the index the entry would have had, while dispatchLogs on a StoreLogs error only answers the futures and steps the node down. The in-memory latest configuration therefore describes a log entry that does not exist, and because quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState all read that latest configuration, a leader that failed to remove a voter can re-elect itself with the smaller quorum and commit alone.
investigations.discriminator: Two real voters with a store that fails exactly the configuration write: after the failed RemoveServer, compare the in-memory latest configuration index with the last stored log index, then let the node stand for election and apply a command, and compare the resulting commit index with the last log index on the other voter. A latest index inside the stored log, or a commit that the peer has, would refute the hypothesis.

knowledge.statement: appendConfigurationEntry dispatches the configuration entry with dispatchLogs and then, regardless of whether the entry was stored, sets the latest configuration to the new configuration at the index the entry would have occupied, reconfigures the commitment map and restarts replication; dispatchLogs answers the futures with the store error and moves the node to follower, leaving the in-memory latest configuration ahead of the stored log.
knowledge.conditions: Leader applying a configuration change whose StoreLogs call fails.

knowledge.statement: quorumSize, electSelf and setupLeaderState all derive their voter set and quorum from the node's latest configuration, so a latest configuration that is not present in the log governs elections and commitment for that node.
knowledge.conditions: Any node whose configurations.latest refers to an unstored configuration entry.

scope.description: One two-voter cluster of real nodes over in-memory transports. The leading member's log store fails exactly the write carrying the configuration entry that would remove the other voter. The harness records the configuration index the leader holds afterwards against its last stored log index, then waits for the node to lead again and applies one client command, comparing the resulting commit index with the other voter's last log index.
assumptions: Both members run the captured code with 300 ms heartbeat, election and lease timeouts and share no state.
The injected failure is a single StoreLogs call returning an error; the store is otherwise the standard in-memory store and accepts later writes.
The harness does not assert which of the two members becomes leader first; it targets whichever one leads when the failure is injected.
A command is treated as committed when its Apply future returns nil, which is the client-visible completion point.
excluded: No restart of the failed node, so the log-derived configuration that would replace the phantom one is not exercised.
No snapshot, no third member and no concurrent client traffic.

experiment.prefix: The harness creates two in-memory transports connected to each other, bootstraps the same two-voter configuration on both stores, and starts both rafts with 300 ms timeouts. It waits for a leader, arms that leader's log store to fail the next StoreLogs call, and calls RemoveServer for the other member. It records the returned error, the node's state, the in-memory latest configuration index and servers, and the last stored log index, then waits up to ten seconds for the node to be Leader again, applies one command with a three-second timeout, and emits the commit index, the leader's last log index and the other voter's last log index.
experiment.responsibility: The library owns both the durability of a configuration change and the supporter set used for elections and commitment. A configuration entry that was never stored cannot be the configuration under which the node counts votes or commits entries; reporting the change as failed while adopting it for quorums leaves the caller and the cluster with incompatible views of who must agree.

comparisons.description: The failed log write must be reported to the caller as a failure.
The in-memory latest configuration must not refer to an index beyond the stored log.
A client command must not be reported committed unless the committed two-voter configuration's quorum, here both voters, has it; the peer lacking it contradicts this.
